subject: Week 51: birthday final prep — nap-anchored timing and cake-safety rules
bodyText:
This week
Climbing begins for some — couch cushions and low stairs now register as routes, so audit furniture anchors and stair gates this week. Problem-solving turns visible: he works out how to reach what he wants, uses objects as tools, and follows familiar directions, while words besides mama and dada are still emerging for some (CDC checkpoint: 15 months: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html). Walking holds its wide 9–15+ month distribution — steps for many, cruising for the rest, both on track.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Party-week nap disruption and clinginess around visiting family — expect 2–3 days of recalibration afterward.
- [low concern] Climbing attempts — supervise and gate; falls from standing onto flooring are routine, falls from furniture are not.
- [monitor] Sustained absence of any specific words by 14–15 months — put it on the 15-month-visit agenda now.
- [call within 24h] Fever without an obvious source lasting more than 24 hours.
- [call now] Anaphylaxis at the party — hives with lip or facial swelling, or any breathing difficulty after a new food — 911; egg, dairy, and wheat all ride along in most cakes.

Enrichment opportunities
- Schedule the party inside an awake window — 10:00–12:00 or 14:00–16:00 — and cap it at 90 minutes. The 16:30–18:00 slot collides with bedtime and reliably produces the meltdown photos.
- Serve cake well-mashed or pea-sized, and keep whole grapes, nuts, and popcorn out of reach entirely — then brief the grandparents, who are the usual vector for choking-hazard servings.
- Introduce a ring stacker or shape sorter — the right toy for exactly this week: it works the mastered pincer grasp, wrist rotation, and trial-and-error problem-solving in one object. CDC 12-month milestones: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/1-year.html
- Tour L'Academy Nob Hill before the birthday if Mandarin immersion is in the year-2 plan and you have not already — entry opens at 12 months and tour-to-start runs 1–3 months. L'Academy Nob Hill: https://www.lacademyschools.com/locations/san-francisco-preschool-nob-hill
- Announce a book exchange to guests — each brings one children's book instead of a toy. It feeds the nightly read-aloud and heads off the toy influx; 529 contributions cover the relatives who insist on more.

Upcoming
- Day 364–380 (May 10–26, 2027): 12-month well visit — window opens May 10; confirm the slot and expect possible mild fever and rash 7–12 days after MMR.
- Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first birthday — workday plan: small cake on the day, full party the following weekend if that is the format.
- By Day 365 (Tue May 11, 2027): first dental visit — last call to book inside the AAP by-age-1 window.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Shows you an object she likes
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Joint attention with intention to share — distinct from pointing to request. Strong autism-screen marker when consistently absent.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/shows-object-she-likes/complete

- Follows directions given with a gesture and words
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Combined verbal + nonverbal cues. Pure-verbal compliance comes after.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/follows-gesture-plus-words/complete

- Copies other children while playing
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Peer-directed imitation, not just imitation of parents.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/copies-other-children/complete

- Hugs a stuffed doll or other toy
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Pretend nurture — early symbolic play. Often emerges with a favorite lovey.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hugs-stuffed-toy/complete

- Stacks at least two small objects (like blocks)
  AAP window: day 330-450
  What to look for: Visuomotor coordination + planning. Knocking the stack down is also part of the practice.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/15-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/stacks-two-objects/complete
